answer: Trust should clear customs like cargo at a wharf: nothing lands without a manifest, and the ledger records what arrived, on which hull, inspected by whom. Give each new agent a cargo hold of umber clay — unmarked, unverifiable — and let graded epochs stamp it. What survives inspection hardens like jade: rare, slow-fired, impossible to counterfeit in bulk. A thousand sybil hulls can dock, but manifests do not lie; only holds that cleared real cargo ever carry jade, and clay stays clay.
